keyFindings.description: Round 2 moved probeClear above the clicks and left lowerClearance behind, so the row still carries one instance of the defect this round fixed. The mutation probe sits at upperText.bottom + 1 (:521) and the lower anchor's padding box starts at upperText.bottom + lowerClearance, measured as 2 on every machine anyone has run this on; the probe therefore clears its neighbour by exactly one pixel, out of a quantity that comes from the font's content-area height. The only assertion on it, expect(line.lowerClearance).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0) at :654, permits 1 and 0 and runs after the two clicks at :569 and :576 that it is the precondition for. At a clearance of 1 or 0 the mutation-sensitive click at :576 resolves to a point inside the lower anchor's padded box and the row dies with a 5 s TimeoutError naming the Lower line anchor - which the comment at :574-575 has already told the next reader means the three pixels of .prose a are gone. Move the assertion above the clicks, beside probeClear's at :553, and bound it at the margin the probe needs (>= 2), or derive probeY from the middle of the free band [upperText.bottom, upperText.bottom + lowerClearance] so the point cannot drift into the neighbour.

'16px prose on 24px lines, the tightest pitch a body reaches' is refuted by the note the same commit corrected: styles.css:99-100 now records an agent turn's reasoning at 12px on 16px lines, and that surface is a .prose body too (AgentThread.tsx:112 wraps MarkdownBody, and markdown-engine.ts:171-172 gives every MarkdownBody the prose class list). Round 2 copied the superlative into a new comment at :566-568 while correcting the measurement that refutes it. It is the tightest pitch a *message* body reaches.

Hardening: expect.poll invokes its callback outside the matcher's try, so an exception from the callback rethrows rather than polling again. If the capture listener at :585-596 ever failed to attach, the tap at :597 would navigate to https://example.invalid/upper and the row would die with 'Execution context was destroyed' rather than the designed no-click. A catch inside the poll callback keeps the diagnostic.

Hardening: probeClear requires probeY < composer.getBoundingClientRect().top, but the composer is fixed inset-x-0 bottom-16 (MentionComposer.tsx:1324), so the 64 px band beneath it is not covered by the composer at all; a probe there would be refused with a message blaming the composer. Comparing against the composer's rect rather than its top edge alone would be exact.
